title: Technical Support in Formulation of the Building Sustainable, Inclusive, and Climate-Resilient Tourism in Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands Project Targeting the Adaptation Fund
description: Global Green Growth Institute in Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands is inviting all eligible companies to submit their bids for consulting services to provide technical support in Formulation of the Building Sustainable, Inclusive, and Climate-Resilient Tourism in Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands Project Targeting the Adaptation Fund.ABOUT GGGI:The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) was established as an intergovernmental organization with the objective of promoting sustainable development of developing and emerging countries including the least developed countries. GGGI is dedicated to supporting the creation and diffusion of the model of economic growth known as “green growth”. The green growth model integrates economic growth, environmental sustainability, poverty reduction and social inclusion.PROJECT BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVES:The GGGI began its operations in Papua New Guinea (PNG) and the Solomon Islands in 2018 and 2019, respectively. Since then, the GGGI has implemented several projects in PNG funded by various donors which include the establishment of the Climate Resilient Green Growth Project (CRGG), Infrastructure for Resilient Island States PNG Project, and Climate Finance Initiative for Resilience and Sustainable Transition (Climate FIRST). Similarly, the key achievements in the Solomon Islands include the launch of the Solomon Islands Low Emission Development Strategy in 2023, and the implementation of Strengthening Inclusive Adaptation Capacity in Solomon Islands (SIAC-SI) project, among others. By supporting these initiatives, GGGI aims to enhance both countries’ resilience to climate change and promote sustainable, inclusive growth. Notwithstanding setbacks caused by the COVIND-19 pandemic, the GoPNG and the GoSL are dedicated to building sustainable and inclusive tourism sectors. In PNG, tourism accounts for about 1.9% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and employs about 25,0001 people. In addition to increasing the numbers of visitors, PNG also plans to significantly increase the number of jobs in tourism up to 310,000 by 2030. In the Solomon Islands, prior to the pandemic, tourism represented 10.5% of GDP and generated US$132.8 million2. Tourism is a key source of income diversification, especially for remote and coastal communities. Both countries heavily rely on vulnerable coastal ecosystems, cultural heritage, and community-based enterprises, which are threatened by climate change impacts. Tourism has been hit hard by the intensifying and increased frequency of climate change impacts such as rising sea levels, more acidic oceans, floods, saltwater intrusion, droughts, and heat waves. These climate hazards are threatening coastal tourism infrastructure, natural attractions, and the viability of some eco-tourism ventures. Key stakeholders in both countries often lack awareness, knowledge, technical capacity, and financial resources to avoid or minimize their exposure to disaster and climate risks. Moreover, women and youth are underrepresented in tourism leadership and face barriers to accessing finance, technology, and training. Given the increased impacts of climate change, the efforts to foster more resilience in the tourism sector need to be scaled up. In light of the above, the GoPNG and GoSL, in collaboration with GGGI, have agreed to work together to develop a regional project proposal targeting the Adaptation Fund. The Building Sustainable, Inclusive, and Climate-Resilient Tourism in Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands Project seeks to foster climate-smart tourism pathways by strengthening governance and institutional frameworks, improving access to climate information and early warning systems (CIEWS), promoting inclusive tourism enterprises, and restoring ecosystems through nature-based solutions (NbS). By mainstreaming climate change adaptation into the tourism sector, the project will enhance national and local resilience while safeguarding critical ecosystems, preserving the culture and identity, reducing vulnerability to climate hazards, and unlocking new opportunities for green and inclusive growth in PNG and the Solomon Islands. In PNG, the proposed project will target New Ireland, Milne Bay and East New Britain Provinces. Whereas, in the Solomon Island the project will target Western, Central and Malaita Provinces. The Purpose of this Consultancy is as follows: • Establish a comprehensive baseline of socio-economic, environmental, gender and social inclusion, and institutional conditions in the tourism sector of PNG and the Solomon Islands. • Identify existing vulnerabilities of tourism-dependent communities, particularly women and youth, to climate change impacts. • Map ongoing tourism-related initiatives, and policies to avoid duplication and identify synergies. • Generate baseline indicators aligned with the project’s results framework to enable effective monitoring and evaluation throughout the project cycle.• Develop a full-fledged quality Concept Note (CN) for the Adaptation Fund (AF) for the project titled Building Sustainable, Inclusive, and Climate-Resilient Tourism in Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands Project• Ensure the CN is fully aligned with the relevant AF guidelines and template requirements, demonstrating strong alignment with AF’s strategic priorities, investment criteria, and expectations• Provide technical support during the review process of the CN including revision and strengthening of the CN by addressing comments and feedback received from the Adaptation Fund Secretariat.PROPOSED ACTIVITIES & SCOPE OF WORK:The selected firm will carry out the following tasks to establish a comprehensive baseline and recommendations:Proposed Activities: 1. Inception Meeting and Work Plan Development:o Conduct a virtual kick-off meeting with key stakeholders including the Secretariat of the Pacific Regional Environment Programme (SPREP) SPREP and the Pacific Tourism Organization (SPTO) to discuss priorities and past/ ongoing activities in the PNG and the Solomon Islands as well as the regional developments, which may be relevant to better understand the project and alignment o Review and assess relevant policy documents, existing studies, reports, and data to gain more insight into tourism sector, livelihoods, and ecosystem-based adaptation to climate change in both countrieso Identify gaps in existing data to inform the baseline assessment and CN formulationo Prepare and submit a concise Inception Report detailing the firm's understanding of the scope, proposed streamlined methodology, detailed work plan aligned with the 4-month timeline, proposed stakeholder engagement strategy, and schedule of deliverables. Include assumptions and dependencies regarding focal points, data access and logistical arrangements. Deliverable 1: An inception report 2. Stakeholder, Financial, and Baseline Assessments o Identify and map all relevant stakeholders, including community groups, government agencies, and the private sector, involved in the tourism in PNG, and in the Solomon Islands. o Clarify the stakeholders’ interests/goals/objectives and categorize them based on their interests for sustainable tourism. o Map the geographical locations of the different stakeholders’ activities and, if possible, include the current and planned or approved budget allocations. o Map government departments, including district and divisional levels, along with their plans and how their contributions and needs can be incorporated into the proposed project. o Map how the private sector would engage in the project through public-private partnerships and knowledge sharing. o Identify and map out the different target sites for each activity per province in PNG and Solomon Islands.o Conduct stakeholder consultations, through interviews, focus groups, and surveys to gather feedback on the proposed project. The consultations should among other aspects, include gender views on challenges or issues women are facing in tourism space and climate risks that the proposed project can help address. o Facilitate focus group discussions with women, youth, and marginalized groups in selected pilot tourism sites and communities. o Assess the condition of existing and planned tourism infrastructure, services, and natural resource management systems. o Collect data to establish baseline values for project indicators (e.g number of women/youth in tourism livelihoods, hectares of ecosystems protected). o Identify gaps in institutional capacity, climate information and early warning, and community engagement. o Compare vulnerability profiles between PNG and the Solomon Islands. o Identify capacity/training as well as technological needs (in terms of availability in the area, cost of the technology, and back up service) which should be prioritized under the projecto Conduct a financial analysis to estimate the net economic value of proposed project interventions in PNG and Solomon Islands, incorporating direct tourism benefits, ecosystem service values, gender/youth livelihood improvements, and avoided climate-related losses. Deliverable 2: Stakeholder Consultation Summary & Preliminary Needs Assessment Report, Financial assessment as well as a draft Baseline assessment report with key data 3. Adaptation Fund Concept Note (Regional Project) DevelopmentUsing the final report of the stakeholder and baseline assessments, the consultant will undertake the following activities: a) Draft fully-developed AF Concept Note, meeting minimum requirements by the Adaptation Fund for validationo Prepare the draft Concept Note for the project titled: “Building Sustainable, Inclusive, and Climate-Resilient Tourism in Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands Project”. o The Project Concept Note shall meet the minimum requirements of the Adaptation Fund CN with clear clarifications of, but not limited to, the following components: o Adaptation rationale by clearly presenting adaptation challenges that need to be addressed o Proposed objectives and interventions o Alignment with country priorities and policies - Ensure the CN reflects national climate adaptation goals, institutional mandates, and policy frameworks. GGGI will facilitate communication between the consultant and key stakeholders. o Alignment with AF results framework o Screening of environmental and social safeguards in line with the AF and SPREP ESS requirementsb) Feedback and revision o Incorporate inputs from GGGI, Implementing Entity, and relevant government stakeholders in both countries, into the final version of the CN.o Ensure technical, institutional, and policy coherence. o Conduct a short debrief with GGGI to share lessons learned and identify any potential opportunities or ideas for future project development that emerged during the assignment. o Respond to comments and feedback received from the AF c) Response to Adaptation Fund Comments (1 round) o Respond to comments and technical feedback received from the Adaptation Fund following initial CN submission for up to 1 round of revisions. o Revise CN as needed in coordination with GGGI and SPREP, ensuring clarity, technical robustness, and full compliance. Deliverable 3: Quality AF Concept Note developed and submitted Methodology Guidance: The firm is encouraged to propose a lean, efficient, and highly consultative methodology that maximizes the use of existing information and prioritizes virtual engagements where appropriate to optimize the limited budget and timeline.
